::: {.solutions}

**Show all your reasoning.** Total: **32 marks** · Suggested time: **45 minutes**.

Two rules settle every negation below:

$$\text{not}(\text{for all } x,\ P) = \text{there exists } x,\ \text{not } P \qquad\qquad
\text{not}(\text{there exists } x,\ P) = \text{for all } x,\ \text{not } P$$

**Flip the quantifier, and negate the inside — both, every time.**

| Section | What it covers | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Fluency** | truth of quantified statements; single negations | 10 |
| **B — Exam standard** | counterexamples; negating conditions inside | 14 |
| **C — Stretch** | two quantifiers and their order | 8 |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Also due this session:** Notes on Logic and Proof, **pp. 56–63**, plus **five "for all" statements of
your own** about integers (three true, two false, with counterexamples for the false ones).
:::

# Section A — Fluency

## Question 1 **[4]**

State whether each is **true** or **false**. In each case $x$ is real, $n$ an integer.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) For all real $x$, &nbsp; $x^2 + 1 > 0$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) There exists a real $x$ such that $x^2 = -1$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) For all integers $n$, &nbsp; $2n$ is even. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(d) There exists an integer $n$ such that $n^2 = 2$. **[1]**

# Section B — Exam standard

## Question 4 **[6]**

For each statement, decide whether it is true. If false, **disprove it with a counterexample**; if true,
give a one-line reason.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) For all real $x$, &nbsp; $\sqrt{x^2} = x$. **[2]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) For all real $x$, &nbsp; if $x > 3$ then $x^2 > 9$. **[2]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) For all integers $n$, &nbsp; $n^2 - n$ is even. **[2]**

## Question 6 **[4]**

$n$ denotes a positive integer. Consider the statement

$$\textbf{(S):}\quad \text{For all } n, \text{ if } n \text{ is a multiple of } 6 \text{ then } n \text{ is a multiple of } 3.$$

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Is (S) true? Justify. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Write the negation of (S). **[2]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) Does a counterexample to (S) exist? If so give one; if not, explain why. **[1]**

# Section C — Stretch

## Question 7 **[5]**

For positive integers, consider:

&nbsp;&nbsp;**P:** For all $m$, there exists $n$ such that $n > m$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**Q:** There exists $n$ such that for all $m$, $n > m$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Explain the difference in meaning between **P** and **Q**. **[2]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) State, with reasons, whether each is true. **[2]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) Write the negation of **Q**. **[1]**

::: {.callout-tip}
## Before you hand this in

Check every negation twice: did you **flip the quantifier** *and* **negate the inside**? A negation that
changed only one of the two is the commonest error in this whole topic — and it is exactly what is being
marked.
:::
